correctness.rationale: The two recurrences equal unmarked odd binary partition counts and the marked moment sum; the checker independently verifies this up to N=129. The proof bounds f(N) between 2^{m²/2-O(m log m)} and 2^{m²/2+O(m)}, then bounds the fraction of partitions with at most (1-epsilon)m occupied positive levels by 2^{-epsilon²m²/2+O(m log m)}. The size-biasing moment is squeezed between (1-o(1))2^{(1-epsilon)m} and 2^m for each epsilon>0, yielding log(p/f)/log N→1. All quantifiers restrict to positive odd N→infinity; no finite experiment is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The 2023 motivating paper explicitly poses comparison of odd-indexed growth rates. Determining the full exponent one for the ratio p(N)/f(N), while both counts have the same leading quadratic logarithmic scale, provides a structural answer for a natural pair rather than a small table or routine coefficient substitution. Near-full occupied-level concentration is the key reusable lemma. It does not solve the finer constant-level comparison or other self-similar families.
